This manual details how to command, test, and control the Claw Telegram bot directly from your VS Code PowerShell (pwsh) terminal.

1. BASIC DIRECT COMMS (SENDING MESSAGES TO YOUR TELEGRAM)
---------------------------------------------------------
Use the OpenClaw message utility to send direct text alerts from your PowerShell terminal to your Telegram client:

* Send via your raw Telegram User ID (Fast & Reliable):
  openclaw message send --channel telegram --target "8561862929" --message "Claw: System check initiated. All systems green."

* Send via your Telegram Username:
  openclaw message send --channel telegram --target "@james_hooper1973" --message "Claw: Warning — 15:00 publication was missed and manually caught up."

2. READING & POLLING TELEGRAM CHATS FROM PWSH
---------------------------------------------
You can inspect recent messages, read chat trajectories, or poll for responses directly from the console:

* Read the last 10 messages from your Telegram chat:
  openclaw message read --channel telegram --target "8561862929" --limit 10

* Check active session states and channels:
  openclaw sessions list

* Tail live logs of the background gateway:
  openclaw sessions tail

3. TESTING PAIRING & SECURITY STATUS
------------------------------------
If you get access configuration issues, use these commands to verify that your identity is registered and approved:

* Check paired devices and tokens:
  openclaw devices list

* View current allowFrom list (authorized senders):
  Get-Content "C:\Users\peteh\.openclaw\credentials\telegram-default-allowFrom.json"

* Approve a new pairing code:
  openclaw pairing approve telegram <CODE>

4. AUTOMATING SCRIPT ALERTS IN PWSH
-----------------------------------
You can wire Claw alerts into your custom PowerShell scripts (like cron triggers or watchdogs). 

Example PowerShell snippet to trigger a Telegram alert if a process fails:
```powershell
# Alert claw on Telegram if nginx is down
$NginxCheck = Test-Connection -ComputerName "localhost" -Port 80 -Quiet
if (-not $NginxCheck) {
    openclaw message send --channel telegram --target "8561862929" --message "⚠️ ALERT: Nginx on port 80 is unreachable! Triggering rebuild."
}
```
